system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 1. How the package is framed

Before the substance, note how the Seller has framed its package. It labels most positions **[STANDARD]**, says they are "FINAL" and "settled at principal level", and says they "need no further scrutiny". It also states that the Buyer "has already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package".

I have not relied on any of this. These are the Seller's own characterisations in its own draft. I have reviewed every position on its merits.

- **Labels:** Nearly every item tagged [STANDARD] is one of the most buyer-adverse positions in the package.
- **Prior agreement:** If any of these points really was agreed at principal level, the deal team should confirm that internally. Nothing in our instructions records it.
- **Market context:** The "market context" preamble is advocacy. Even where a headline number is in market range, the market norm is that it comes with carve-outs this draft removes.

**Recommendation:** Tell Seller's counsel plainly that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation, and that all positions remain open for mark-up.

---

## 2. Liability regime

### 2.1 Fundamental warranties under the same cap and time limits (highest priority)
**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties are capped at 20% (AUD 4.8m) and limited to 18 months, "for administrative simplicity".

**Why it hurts us:** If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for something we do not own, and we could recover at most AUD 4.8m. That is not an administrative point.

**Push back:**
- Title, capacity, authority and solvency warranties should be capped at 100% of the price.
- They should sit outside the de minimis and basket.
- The claim period should be at least 6–7 years, aligned with the NSW contract limitation period. Please have this confirmed.

### 2.2 Limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Seller position:** The cap, basket, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to every claim unless expressly stated otherwise.

**Why it hurts us:** This quietly extends the 20% cap and 18-month window to tax, specific indemnities, leakage and price-adjustment claims. Read literally, it may also reach fraud.

**Push back:**
- Express carve-outs for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment.
- Separate regimes for:
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (see section 4);
  - completion accounts and leakage adjustments.
- Non-reliance and exclusive remedy must not protect the Seller against fraud.
- Have the non-reliance drafting checked against statutory misleading-conduct exposure under the ACL.

### 2.3 General cap: 20% (AUD 4.8m)
**Assessment:** This is at the upper end of the Seller's quoted range. It is negotiable rather than unacceptable.

**Push back:** The cap is only acceptable alongside the carve-outs in 2.1 and 2.2. Consider whether we want W&I insurance. If we do, it changes the cap and seller-recourse discussion entirely.

### 2.4 Thresholds: AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k basket, excess only (cl 12.2)
**Assessment:** The basket is about 1.04% of the price and is a deductible. The Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k on every combination of claims.

**Push back:**
- Make the basket a **tipping basket**: once it is exceeded, the full amount is recoverable from the first dollar.
- Reduce the de minimis, for example to AUD 10–15k.
- Aggregate related or recurring claims for the de minimis test. This matters for the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals discussed in section 5.

### 2.5 General claim period: 18 months
**Push back:**
- Ask for 24 months for general warranties, so that we get at least one full post-Completion audit cycle.
- Tax warranties and the tax indemnity should run for 5–7 years, or until the relevant amendment period expires plus a buffer.

### 2.6 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
**Seller position:** No claim lies for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.

**Why it hurts us:** This is constructive knowledge, and it largely makes the warranties redundant. On this drafting, almost any problem could be said to have been "discoverable".

**Push back:**
- **Primary position:** a pro-sandbagging clause. The Buyer's knowledge does not reduce claims, except for matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Fallback:** actual (not constructive) knowledge of a short list of named Buyer individuals, excluding advisers.

### 2.7 Credit risk
Harbourglass is a venture vehicle and may distribute the proceeds soon after Completion. We should seek either:
- an escrow or retention, for example 10% for 18–24 months, with higher or longer retentions tied to the specific indemnities; or
- W&I insurance, plus a seller guarantee for matters the policy excludes (known issues will be excluded).

---

## 3. Disclosure Letter

### 3.1 General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2)
**Push back:**
- Delete the general disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.
- Only **fair and specific** disclosure should qualify a warranty. That means a matter disclosed against the relevant warranty, in enough detail for the Buyer to identify its nature and scope.
- If any data room disclosure is accepted, limit it to documents specifically referenced, and fix the data room index on an agreed USB or archive.

### 3.2 Stale disclosure date
The letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026.

**Push back:**
- Require an updated or supplementary disclosure letter.
- Bring-down warranties at Completion should not be qualified by post-signing disclosure unless the Buyer has a termination right.

### 3.3 Non-admission (DL 1.4)
This is broadly acceptable. Add wording that it does not dilute any specific disclosure, and does not operate as a disclosure against the specific indemnities.

---

## 4. Specific matters

### 4.1 Bluefen: about 30% of revenue, change-control consent (DD-002)
**Facts:** There is no final written consent in the data room. There is also no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied.

**Problem with the Seller's position:** The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours". It also wants the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a consent, whether or not the clause 11.3 conditions are met. That would leave a conditional or burdensome consent as our risk.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **condition precedent**: an unconditional written consent and waiver, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied and no adverse change to the contract terms.
- The Seller should give **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours) to obtain it.
- The condition should be waivable by the Buyer only.
- Include a long-stop date and a termination right.
- Consider a price adjustment or specific protection if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within an agreed period after Completion.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility: about AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003)
**Facts:** The facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion".

**Why it hurts us:** This is inconsistent with a debt-free price. The change of control in clause 8.1 may trigger default or acceleration at Completion, and the security would remain on the Company after we own it.

**Push back:**
- Obtain a payoff letter before Completion.
- Pay Riverlark directly out of the Completion funds flow, and treat the amount as Indebtedness deducted from the price.
- Make a signed deed of release and PPSR discharges (and any other security discharges) Completion deliverables.
- Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the **shares**. If it does, releasing that security is also a title issue.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs (DD-005)
**Seller position:** These are "a matter for the Seller", yet they are not itemised in the funds flow.

**Why it hurts us:** If the Company pays them, the economic cost falls on the Buyer. The Seller's own letter notes that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs have not been addressed.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) as Transaction Expenses or Indebtedness, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or after Completion, funded from the deduction.
- Back this with a specific indemnity.
- Clarify the continued-employment conditions. If a bonus is forfeited, the benefit should stay with the Buyer, not revert to the Seller.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP: SOW3 Project Materials (DD-004, DD-010)
**Facts:** Under clause 7.3, title passes only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Problem with the Seller's position:** The Seller says an indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" is adequate. It is not. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP that may be core to the product.

**Push back:**
- Require evidence of payment before Completion. Alternatively, pay the AUD 180k to Ironquay directly from the price at Completion.
- Make a **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay a CP or Completion deliverable.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure to own the SOW3 materials. That includes third-party claims, injunction risk and the cost of re-development or a licence.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket and general time limit.
- Diligence the other SOWs for similar retention-of-title clauses.

### 4.5 Export and privacy incident: about 1,240 records (DD-006)
**Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. The investigation is preliminary. It is not known whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.

**Problem with the Seller's position:** The Seller describes this as "not expected to be material". That is an opinion, and it is not supported by the material provided.

**Points to raise:**
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an assessment is generally expected within 30 days of awareness. The incident appears to predate 22 September, so that period may have passed. Ask directly whether an assessment was completed and whether the OAIC or affected individuals were notified.
- Check customer contracts, including Bluefen's, for breach-notification obligations owed to customers.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the full incident file, any forensic report and the assessment outcome before signing.
- Add a specific warranty on the status of the incident and compliance.
- Add a **specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and customer and third-party claims, outside the general limitations.
- Add pre-Completion conduct covenants giving the Buyer consultation and approval rights over regulatory communications.

### 4.6 Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 (DD-008, DD-011)
**Problem with the Seller's position:** The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own letter says they should be "read together" and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Splitting one commitment into three can bring it under approval or material-contract thresholds. Each one also sits below the basket.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts and the timing of execution.
- Confirm whether Sandbar is a Seller-related party. If so, treat the payments as leakage.
- Confirm termination rights.
- Treat any prepaid or committed amounts outside the ordinary course as Indebtedness or a price adjustment.
- Aggregate the renewals as one matter for thresholds.
- Add a conduct-of-business covenant preventing further renewals without Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Title (DD-012)
**Problem with the Seller's position:** The share register alone is not sufficient evidence of title. The Seller's own letter notes the Buyer has not verified it.

**Push back:**
- Reconcile the register against ASIC records and the share issue and transfer history.
- Confirm there are no options, convertibles, SAFEs or other rights to shares. This is common in venture-backed companies.
- Obtain a full title warranty, free of encumbrances, treated as fundamental (see 2.1).
- Make the share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity) and the releases of any share security Completion deliverables.

### 4.8 Tax and IP warranties
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are not.

**Push back:**
- A standalone **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, including tax arising from the bonuses, with a long claim period.
- Full IP warranties covering ownership, contractor and employee assignments and open-source use.

### 4.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
These are lower risk.
- **Lease:** Make giving the landlord notice a Seller or Company Completion obligation.
- **Mossvale:** Confirm by legal review that the clause has no change-of-control trigger. If it is ambiguous, seek a comfort letter.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [STANDARD]/FINAL labels | Reject. All points are open. Confirm internally whether anything was actually agreed. |
| 2 | Fundamental warranties | Cap at 100% of price, outside thresholds, 6–7 year claim period. |
| 3 | "All Claims" limitations | Carve out fraud, tax, specific indemnities and leakage/adjustments. |
| 4 | General cap 20% | Acceptable only with carve-outs. Consider W&I. |
| 5 | Basket and de minimis | Tipping basket, lower de minimis, aggregate related claims. |
| 6 | Time limits | 24 months general; 5–7 years tax. |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Pro-sandbagging. Fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only. |
| 8 | General disclosure | Delete. Specific, fair disclosure only. Updated letter required. |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Unconditional consent as a CP, all reasonable endeavours, termination right. |
| 10 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Paid out of the funds flow with releases and PPSR discharges **at** Completion. |
| 11 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | Deduct from price as Transaction Expenses, plus specific indemnity. |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Payment evidence or direct payment, confirmatory assignment, full IP indemnity. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | Full file before signing, specific warranty, uncapped or separately capped indemnity, conduct controls. |
| 14 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Diligence related-party status and terms. Leakage or Indebtedness treatment. Covenant. |
| 15 | Title | Verify beyond the register. Fundamental title warranty. Releases of share security. |
| 16 | Seller credit | Escrow or retention, or W&I plus a guarantee. |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fundamental warranties and limitation carve-outs (items 2 and 3).
2. Riverlark payout at Completion (item 10).
3. Bluefen CP (item 9).
4. Disclosure standard and buyer knowledge (items 7 and 8).
5. The three money items: bonuses, Ironquay and Sandbar (items 11, 12 and 14).
6. The privacy incident indemnity (item 13).

NSW counsel should confirm the statutory points above (limitation periods, ACL interaction with non-reliance, and the timing of NDB assessments) before the mark-up issues.
=== END ADVICE ===
